newsitem.title: USA: Stocks retreat as bonds trim gains. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Stocks retreat as bonds trim gains. [CORRECTED 18:40 GMT]

text.p: Stock prices slid Wednesday as a volatile bond market (corrects from "ailing bond market") stood in the way of attempts to reverse the previous day's losses.
At 1:00 p.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the Dow Jones industrial average was off 25.55 points at 7,935.29 after giving back a gain of nearly 80 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances by a small margin on active volume of 352 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 3.30 point at 1,579.54.
"The issues that whipsawed the market today was the economic releases and the bond market," said Robert Froehlich, chief investment strategist at Kemper Funds.
"We dodged the bullet with the PPI number so I think all focus shifts gear to tomorrow to the CPI," he said.
But the bond market was calling the shots, as it swung erratically due to a weak dollar.
The dollar sank to 1.8345 German marks from 1.8630 marks in late New York trading on Tuesday.
A smaller-than-expected rise in July retail sales and a seventh straight monthly drop in producer prices triggered an early jump in bonds that fizzled just as the Dow surged after its opening.
The benchmark 30-year bond was up 10/32 after soaring more than a full point at first on good news about inflation. Its yield dipped to 6.65 percent from Tuesday's close at 6.67 percent.

Stocks burst into the plus column from the opening after the government reported that the Producer Price index -- one of the key gauges of inflation -- dropped unexpectedly for a record seventh month in a row in July
The PPI was off 0.1 percent, following an identical drop in June. Without the volatile food and energy components, wholesale prices also fell by 0.1 percent.
Wall Street analysts surveyed by Reuters had expected prices to rise by 0.1 percent last month.
In a separate report, the Commerce Department said July retail sales were up a moderate 0.6 percent last month, reflecting a broadbased improvement in all businesses except furniture.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.7 percent rise in overall retail sales.

The reports will be among the data considered by Federal Reserve policy-makers next week when they decide whether economic growth is strong enough to require a rise in interest rates in a pre-emptive move against inflation.
The slide in the dollar in Europe against the German mark was having some effect on stocks as it weighed on bonds, but this was downplayed by some analysts.

Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross, said bond prices had been rising on the assumption that the economy would remain relatively slow and that interest rates should come down.
"Now we are seeing signs that maybe the economy is a little stronger," he said.
The volatility will come from stocks taking their cue from bonds and economic data in the absence of any major earnings reports, analysts said.
On Thursday, the government will report on inflation at the consumer level for July, but few analysts expect any bad surprises after Wednesday's upbeat producer price data.

Among individual stocks, Micron Technologies shed 7-1/8 to 43 after Merrill Lynch cut its profit estimates for the company. Other brokers also cut their earnings forecasts, citing falling prices for memory chips.
But Applied Materials Inc., the biggest manufacturer of chip-making equipment, surged after stronger-than-expected earnings were reported. The stock was up 8-1/2 at 98-3/4.
